heroHeadline: Operation Sindoor Turns One: Modi Leads National Tribute, IAF Releases Strike Footage; DG ISPR Warns India of 'Greater Strength'
heroSubtitle: On May 7, 2026 — the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor — both India and Pakistan mounted competing national commemorations. PM Modi changed his profile picture on X, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp to an Operation Sindoor tribute graphic, declaring India 'remains as steadfast as ever' against terrorism; the Indian Air Force released previously unseen strike footage timed to the exact hour of the May 7, 2025 launches. Pakistan's DG ISPR Lt Gen Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry held a major press conference flanked by senior Navy and Air Force officers, declaring Pakistan 'proved its strength against a 5-times bigger enemy' and that any future 'hostile design' would be met with 'greater strength, precision and resolve.' Pakistan simultaneously claims India's attempt to label Pakistan a terror state has been 'buried forever.' The ceasefire is technically holding one year on, but analysts at The Diplomat and Carnegie assess escalation dynamics as elevated: Pakistan's Army has conducted 10+ consecutive days of unprovoked LoC firing in early May — the most intense ceasefire breakdown since the 2021 DGMO agreement. The bilateral freeze remains total: airspace closed until May 24, Indus Waters Treaty suspended, all trade halted ($4B Pakistan trade deficit in April 2026), no ambassadors exchanged.
footerNote: Data sourced from Indian MEA/MOD, Pakistan ISPR/MFA, UN Security Council, SIPRI, Crisis Group, HRW, Stimson Center
